questions.prompt: You configure `mock.method.side_effect = TimeoutError('slow')`. What happens when the code calls the method?

options.text: It raises TimeoutError, letting you test the error path
It records the call but returns None

questions.explanation: Setting side_effect to an exception makes the call raise it, so you can test how your code handles the failure.

questions.prompt: When is a fake a better choice than stubbing each call by hand?

options.text: When the collaborator is stateful — you write then read, or run a sequence
When you make exactly one canned read
When you only want to verify a method was called

questions.explanation: A fake tracks state naturally, so it beats brittle per-call stubs for stateful collaborators like repositories.

questions.prompt: Stubs and fakes support ____ verification — you assert on the result or resulting state, not on which calls were made.
questions.explanation: Stubs and fakes go with state verification; mocks/spies go with behavior verification.

questions.prompt: Which are accurate about fakes? Select all that apply.

options.text: A fake is a working but simplified implementation, often in-memory
A fake must stay faithful to real behavior on the parts you depend on
A contract test can run the same checks against fake and real to prevent drift
A fake never actually stores or computes anything

questions.explanation: Fakes really work (just simplified), must stay faithful, and can be guarded by contract tests; one that 'never stores anything' is a stub, not a fake.

questions.prompt: Match each tool/term to its role.

pairs.right: A Mock's canned return for a call
Make a Mock raise or return a sequence
Keeps a fake in sync with the real implementation

questions.explanation: return_value and side_effect configure stubs; an in-memory repo is a fake; contract tests prevent fake drift.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to test a write-then-read workflow with a fake.

items.text: Build an in-memory fake and seed any starting state
Run the code that writes and reads through the fake
Assert the fake's end state is correct

questions.explanation: Create the fake, exercise the workflow, then verify the resulting stored state.
